messages:
alejandra: Quick morning sync 101212 ran a focused bring-up for pioneer-13b: fp16 vs int8 vs a new mixed-int5 prototype on a 1.2k slice set (short chat, multi-bullet extraction, long summaries, numeric-normalization). Dropping a concise GTN/product handoff + suggested router snippet. Full bench link: https://internal.redwood/bench/pioneer-5024

tom: can you paste a tiny scorecard we can show product? keep it snackable.

alejandra: Scorecard (1.2k mixed):
```
metric             | fp16   | int8   | int5   | note
QA F1              | 0.893  | 0.885  | 0.854  | int8 ~0.9% avg loss
Exact Match (EM)   | 0.822  | 0.815  | 0.781  | extraction-sensitive
ROUGE-L (long)     | 0.441  | 0.433  | 0.402  | long summaries degrade more
Latency p50 (ms)   | 112    | 125    | 138    | p95 increases with kv-cache churn
Cost / 1k tokens   | $0.48  | $0.34  | $0.22  | ~29% / ~54% savings vs fp16
Throughput (req/s) | 9.0    | 10.7   | 12.6   | int5 fastest
```
Short note: priming with a 3-token system anchor reduced variance for int8 on short chat; mixed-int5 still drops low-frequency fields in multi-bullet extraction.

keith: which slices are brittle at low precision? any reproducible examples we can add to the handoff?

alejandra: Repro modes: (1) multi-bullet extraction with optional fields, (2) numeric normalization (unit conversions), (3) long coref >700 tokens. Example failing prompt: "From the spec block, output CSV rows: id, threshold_mV, retry_limit" 0% of int5 responses missed threshold_mV on edge cases.

tom: recommended GTN defaults? Product needs a short, non-technical sentence per tier.

alejandra: Draft handoff lines:
- Economy (exploratory): mixed-int5 for lower cost and higher throughput; not for compliance or audit outputs.
- Balanced (default product): int8 for most user-facing flows; good cost/quality trade-off.
- Premium (SLA/critical extraction): fp16 for high-fidelity extraction, embeddings, and longform summaries.
Fallback: shadow a small percent of cheaper tiers to fp16 and auto-fallback on sustained quality deltas.

keith: what's "small percent" and failure thresholds you recommend?

alejandra: Suggested guardrails:
- Shadowing: mirror 1% of int5/int8 production queries to fp16 and compute rolling deltas for EM and QA F1. Alert if delta > 1.5% sustained for 20m.
- Adversarial probes: hourly batch of 200 targeted examples covering multi-bullet extraction and numeric-normalization. Fail if EM drops >3% vs fp16.
- Missing-field detector: simple regexp-based check for extraction endpoints; if missing-field rate >1% for 10m, route 20% -> fp16 and page.
- Latency watch: if int8/int5 p95 > fp16 p95 * 1.3 and error rate increases >20% baseline, throttle economy traffic.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary scheduled -> bench/pioneer-5024-canary: 1.2k requests over 90m. Results will post to #eng-ml/bench-reports.

product-ops: product wants a one-slide blurb and an example router snippet we can paste. can you give both?

alejandra: One-slide blurb (single sentence): "Recommendation: enable int8 by default for most product endpoints (~30% token cost reduction with ~1% average accuracy loss), reserve fp16 for extraction/embeddings/long outputs, and use 1% shadowing + hourly adversarial checks to detect regressions."

Router snippet (pasteable):
```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"name": "premium", "predicate": "tokens>800 || task==\"extraction\" || user_tier==\"sla\"", "model": "pioneer-13b-fp16"},
    {"name": "balanced", "predicate": "user_tier==\"default\" && tokens<=800", "model": "pioneer-13b-int8"},
    {"name": "economy", "predicate": "user_tier==\"trial\"", "model": "pioneer-13b-mixed-int5"}
  ]
}
```

keith: Anything special for embeddings or retrieval flows?

alejandra: Yes 0 for retrieval/semantic-match keep fp16 embeddings in prod; shadow int8 embedding generation at 2% and alert if avg cosine delta > 0.015 sustained 30m.

product-ops: I'll use that wording. Also add the one-liner: "Do not use mixed-int5 for compliance reports or PII extraction; always route those to premium and enable audit logging."

keith: Great. ping me when bench report lands so we can adjust thresholds if the canary shows slice-specific regressions.

alejandra: Will do 44d I'll attach per-slice tables once canary posts.
